year_launched.note: ANCC has offered a Medical-Surgical Nursing exam for decades (predecessor was RN-BC Medical-Surgical Nursing). The MEDSURG-BC credential name itself reflects ANCC's 2018 'Board-Certified' suffix rebrand; a specific launch year for the credential was not located on the issuing body page during this run.

active_certificants.note: Total MEDSURG-BC credential holders reported in 2024 ANCC Certification Data.

eligibility.value: Hold a current, active RN license within a state or territory of the United States (or the professional, legally recognized equivalent in another country); have practiced the equivalent of 2 years full-time as a registered nurse; have a minimum of 2,000 hours of clinical practice in the specialty area of medical-surgical nursing within the last 3 years; and have completed 30 hours of continuing education in medical-surgical nursing within the last 3 years.

exam_format.value: Computer-based, competency-based, multiple-choice. Delivered by Prometric at test centers nationwide and via remote-proctored option. 150 items total (125 scored + 25 pretest), 3-hour time limit. Year-round testing within a 120-day window after approval.
exam_format.note: ANCC primary source explicitly states 150 questions (125 scored + 25 pretest). Internal certs.js shows 175 — see discrepancies below. Page content will trust certs.js per skill rules.

question_count.note: Per ANCC issuing body. certs.js lists 175; discrepancy logged.

passing_score.value: Scaled score of 350 on a 0-500 scale
passing_score.note: ANCC uses a uniform 0-500 scaled score across its certification exams with 350 as the cut score; corroborated across multiple ANCC-cert references.

fee_ana_member.note: Initial certification; price includes $140 non-refundable administrative fee.

fee_retake.note: ANCC standard retake fee. Retake allowed no sooner than 60 days after a failed attempt; maximum three attempts in a 12-month window.

pass_rate_latest.note: In 2024 ANCC certification data: 4,672 examinees; 3,487 passed = ~75% pass rate.

renewal.value: 5-year cycle. Renew by completing 75 hours of continuing education in medical-surgical nursing PLUS at least one additional professional development category (e.g. additional 75 CE hours, 5 semester credits in specialty coursework, 5 clock-hours of presentations, a problem-solving project, publication, research/dissertation/thesis, mentorship of 120+ hours, or precepting), OR by retaking the certification exam.
renewal.note: At least 60 of the 75 CE hours must be formally approved (ANCC, AMA PRA Category 1, or accepted accreditor).

value.disambiguation: Certified Medical-Surgical Registered Nurse from the Medical-Surgical Nursing Certification Board (MSNCB) is the competing med-surg credential. CMSRN requires 2,000 hours over 5 years and a 150-item exam; MEDSURG-BC is the ANCC counterpart requiring 2 years of RN practice plus 30 CE hours in the specialty.

The legacy ANCC credential — MEDSURG-BC is the current rebranded designation following ANCC's 2018 transition from 'RN-BC' to specialty-suffixed 'Board Certified' credentials. Existing RN-BC holders converted at renewal.

Progressive Care Certified Nurse from AACN targets nurses caring for acutely (but not critically) ill adult patients on step-down units. MEDSURG-BC scope is the broader medical-surgical floor; PCCN is more acute.

salary_context.value: U.S. registered nurses earned a median wage of $93,600 in May 2024 (BLS OEWS); national mean was $98,430. Medical-surgical RNs typically fall near this benchmark, with certified med-surg nurses often commanding a modest premium above non-certified peers due to validated specialty competency.

recent_changes.value: Test Content Outline updated effective September 10, 2024 (PDF dated October 29, 2025). Current TCO uses three domains: Assessment and Diagnosis (39%), Planning/Implementation/Evaluation (40%), and Professional Role (21%). ANCC Certification Renewal Requirements handbook effective September 10, 2025 governs the current renewal cycle.
